# Draft:Sustain Awards

----
Sustain Awards is a Spanish manufacturer of sustainable trophies and award plaques, combining minimalist design with ecological engineering for corporate events, sports competitions, and institutional ceremonies. Founded in 2015 in Barcelona, Catalonia, the company produces all its pieces in Spain using primarily recycled and environmentally certified materials, and ships worldwide through its e-commerce platform.
The company is known for combining minimalist design with ecological engineering, and for a per-unit ecolabel system that quantifies the environmental impact of each product against an equivalent trophy manufactured conventionally in China, conducted under ISO 14040 lifecycle assessment standards. Notable commissions include trophies for the Kings League, the C de C National Creativity Awards, the CaixaBank EmprendeXXI startup programme, the cycling race La Vuelta a España, and the web design platform Awwwards.
History
Sustain Awards was established in Barcelona with the aim of providing high-end, design-led, and environmentally responsible trophies to corporate and institutional clients. The company describes itself as having operated for approximately ten years as of the mid-2020s, during which time it expanded from serving local clients to delivering globally.
According to a February 2026 profile published by Marketing Directo, the company originated from a reflection on the contradiction between the creative industry's forward-looking narrative and the material and aesthetic codes of its recognition objects — trophies that, in the company's framing, remained anchored in previous eras of design and manufacturing.
Products and services
Sustain Awards operates two production lines: a ready-to-personalize collection of trophies, plaques, cups, and medals; and a fully custom design and manufacturing service for bespoke projects. Collection products are available from one unit with no minimum order, personalized via full CMYK UV printing, laser engraving, or sand-blasting. Custom trophies are designed and manufactured from scratch, with geometry, material selection, and finish defined from a client brief.
Individual presentation boxes are produced in Pankaster board made from 100% recycled material. Clients including Google, DHL, and the Kings League have required the fully custom design level, where the trophy is conceived as a purpose-built brand object.
Sustainability approach
Materials
Sustain Awards uses a defined set of recycled and responsibly sourced materials across its collection and custom production lines.
* FSC-certified beech wood: sourced from forests certified under FSC standards, guaranteeing responsible forest management. Used for bases, pedestals, and structural elements.
* Post-consumer recycled plastic: a dense, stone-like material obtained from urban plastic waste containers. Used as a sustainable alternative to the natural stone found in conventional trophies.
* Recycled fishing nets: collected through a recovery programme involving Mediterranean fishing cooperatives. Processed into a structural material used in bases and trophy bodies.
* Recycled-content steel sheet: steel with a partial recycled content, used for plaques and decorative elements, finished with water-based non-toxic paint.
* Selected recycled plastics: materials recovered from food packaging, electronics, and household appliances, used in projects with sufficient lead time and volume.
* Water-based non-toxic paint: applied as the finishing layer across metal and plastic surfaces, free of heavy metals and hazardous substances.
* Pankaster recycled board (600 g/m²): used for individual presentation boxes, yielding a cement-effect finish.
For the 2025 La Vuelta a España commission, the trophies were produced in SBR rubber recycled from bicycle tyres — an example of the company's approach of selecting materials tied to the specific narrative of each event.
For the 2026 Awwwards trophies, a cement and concrete blend with recycled rubber aggregate was used to achieve the brutalist aesthetic specified in the design brief.
Ecolabel
Each collection trophy unit carries an ecolabel: a quantified per-unit environmental impact assessment conducted under ISO 14040 standards in partnership with an engineering firm. The label documents CO₂ emissions savings and material toxicity reductions relative to an equivalent trophy manufactured conventionally in China.
Carbon offset
The company reports an annual process of estimating its total carbon footprint and offsetting it, with records cited for 2022 through 2025.
Notable projects
Kings League — Golden Crown Awards and World Cup (2023–2024)
Sustain Awards designed and manufactured two trophy commissions for the Kings League, a seven-a-side football competition founded in Spain by Gerard Piqué and Ibai Llanos. The Golden Crown Awards (2023) are the highest individual recognition of the competition, awarded to the most outstanding figures of each season both on and off the field. The Kings League World Cup trophy (2024) was produced using recycled and eco-friendly materials consistent with the league's environmental positioning. Event Industry News confirmed Sustain Awards as a custom trophy supplier to the Kings League alongside clients including Google and DHL.
C de C National Creativity Awards (2024–2025)
Sustain Awards has produced the trophies for the Premios Nacionales de Creatividad, organized annually by the Club de Creatividad (c de c), described as the most prominent creative industry recognition in Spain and the wider Spanish-speaking world. The 2025 Honor Award was produced in natural alabaster. The 2025 ceremony was held in Madrid, presented by David Broncano, with 1,463 entries received across all categories.
CaixaBank EmprendeXXI Awards (2025)
Sustain Awards supplied the physical trophies for the Premios EmprendeXXI, a startup recognition programme run by CaixaBank through its DayOne division and co-awarded with Spain's national innovation agency ENISA. First launched in 2007, the programme is described by CaixaBank as the longest-running startup award in Spain and Portugal, with over 560 companies supported. The 18th edition (2025) delivered 19 territorial awards across Spain and Portugal plus six national prizes in thematic categories including sustainability and disruptive innovation.
La Vuelta a España (2025)
For the 2025 edition of La Vuelta a España, one of the three Grand Tours of professional road cycling, Sustain Awards designed and manufactured the competition trophies to mark the race's 90th anniversary. The pieces were produced in SBR rubber — 100% recycled from bicycle tyres — transforming a material specific to cycling into the symbolic object of the race. The project was cited by Marketing Directo as an example of material selection driven by the narrative context of an event rather than generic sustainability criteria.
Awwwards (2026)
In January 2026, Awwwards — an international platform recognizing excellence in web design, usability, and online experience — announced that its new official trophies had been manufactured by Sustain Awards. According to the announcement published on the Awwwards website, the design reinterprets the historic Awwwards trophy through a brutalist aesthetic defined by simple geometries and material honesty, using a cement and concrete blend with recycled rubber aggregate. The piece preserves the iconic morphology of the Awwwards trophy while introducing a front-facing "W" in candy gold mirror finish as a single point of contrast against the mineral base. The announcement described Sustain Awards as "a European design-focused trophy manufacturer specialised in sustainable materials and bespoke production for high-profile international competitions."
Markets and presence
Sustain Awards operates as a 100% e-commerce business with production and logistics based in Spain, serving clients globally through localized websites in Spain, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Belgium, Switzerland, Austria, and Portugal, among other markets.
